steps.text: I'll confirm the sizes first. The 20 mm cube is from your request; the hinge sizes are my starting guesses.

dims.label: Hinge pin diameter
dims.note: Sized for PLA on a 0.4 mm nozzle

dims.label: Knuckle clearance (print-in-place gap)
dims.note: Gap that keeps parts from fusing; too tight and it will not fold

steps.text: Sizes confirmed. Next I'll set out the build plan.

assumptions: Eight 20 mm cubes at the corners of a 2x2x2 frame, joined by 12 hinges along the frame edges
Each cube carries three hinge knuckles, one per axis
Hinges print in place with 0.3 mm clearance; pin diameter 3 mm, knuckle length 6 mm (guesses, sheet confirmed)
Printed flat or in the orientation that keeps all hinge pins horizontal
questions: Should the cubes be solid, or hollow with a wall?

steps.text:
I haven't built the model yet, because I don't think the tools can make a print-in-place version that folds.

The plan needs each hinge to be two interlocking knuckles with a 0.3 mm clearance, cut from the cubes and pins. My tools can join and cut solids, but I can't check that the joints move freely before printing. If I build it as solid cubes with pins through them, the parts will fuse and the cube won't fold.

Two options:
- **Separate pieces (reliable):** I print eight 20 mm cubes and the hinge knuckles as loose parts, which you assemble with a pin per joint.
- **Print-in-place attempt (less certain):** I build the knuckles and clearance gaps and check the fit, but you should expect to test-fold the first print and adjust the clearance.

Which do you want?
